edits.title: Reuse fetched evidence across single and batched requests
edits.content: When single and batched fetching share candidate URLs, keep a URL-keyed cache of fetched text. Deduplicate candidate URLs while preserving order, exclude URLs already cached, fetch the remaining URLs together, and associate returned pages with their input URLs. Build extraction evidence from successful cached pages and reuse those same texts for source and verbatim-quote checks. Do not treat failed fetch responses as usable evidence. Reuse a cached rendering only when it covers the information needed for the current extraction.

edits.title: Compare replacement cells with previously verified evidence
edits.content: A follow-up extraction can pass schema and verbatim-quote checks while silently dropping supported parts of an existing value. Before replacing a populated cell, supply its current value and supporting evidence alongside the new evidence, then compare the proposed replacement for lost attributes, qualifiers, or sources. A shorter statement in a navigation list or another person's page does not establish that omitted attributes are false. Preserve stronger person-specific evidence unless new evidence justifies a correction; investigate actual conflicts rather than blindly taking the latest extraction. Stage replacements until this comparison and quote checks pass. A failed corroborating fetch does not invalidate evidence already verified.

proposal.summary: Refine the existing evidence-validation memory to prevent audits from confusing nationality with citizenship or rendered excerpts with summaries. Existing entries already cover the search and fetch signals.

edits.title: Separate quotation provenance, factual support and field meaning
edits.content: Quote membership in model-rendered fetch output does not by itself establish source wording or support for the complete claim. Distinguish source excerpts from explicitly identified summaries, generated labels and assembled passages; do not reject an excerpt solely because the fetch tool renders text. Before recording a positive constraint verdict, verify the entity, applicable time period and every substantive component of the value. Keep extraction and audit prompts aligned with the requested field: explicit national descriptors can support nationality, but do not establish legal citizenship or dual citizenship. Birthplace, ancestry, workplace, flags and unlinked country labels are insufficient substitutes. Preserve supported compound national descriptors without converting them into citizenship claims. Treat audit findings as claims to check against saved evidence and the task contract, not instructions to apply automatically. For composite affiliations, distinguish actual affiliated institutions from parenthetical organizational descriptions before declaring omissions. When sources support different parts of a composite claim, retain an internal claim-to-excerpt mapping and respect the output contract rather than stitching excerpts into a purported verbatim quote. Recheck semantic support after final mutations, even when schema, substring and coverage checks pass.

additional_candidates.description: Audits introduced stricter citizenship requirements and sometimes treated rendered source excerpts or organizational parentheticals as defects; later targeted reviews corrected those interpretations.

decisions.reason: Reviewed all 29 occurrences: the first four are fallback searches returning already discovered people; the next nine verify nationalities; the following eleven target missing nationality, affiliation or motivation evidence; the last five target remaining cells. Their empty discoveries reflect known entities, not premature placeholders. Several searches supplied useful new evidence without new people. Entry 0 already explicitly permits honest empty discovery records for verification searches. Its recurring signals therefore do not establish consistently bad behavior or justify suppressing them.

Reviewed all 26 failures: nine initial same-host failures, six failures in the expanded alternative batch, seven during nationality retrieval, two during gap retrieval and two during final targeted retrieval. The nationality batch retried two previously failed URLs; another URL failed after an earlier successful retrieval, demonstrating why successful versions must be retained. Recovery is observed in successful alternative-host probes and subsequent evidence retrievals. Entry 1's current version already adds probing before large batches, failed-URL tracking, preservation of successful evidence and avoidance of unchanged retries. Usage records identify version 1, so these failures do not demonstrate failure of the revised version 2. No additional fetch rule or inferred outage cause is warranted.

The second audit explicitly demanded citizenship for a nationality column and rejected national labels on that basis. Later prompts clarified that national descriptors were acceptable, and a final review recovered a compound descriptor previously narrowed to one nationality. Reviews also challenged rendered name–institution excerpts and later flagged a parenthetical parent organization; targeted adjudication retained the supported institution cell. These recovered process errors justify clarifying entry 3 rather than adding another memory. Its existing semantic-support safeguards remain useful, and entry 2 already covers quotation repair from saved evidence. Passing citation membership and constraint coverage checks do not resolve these interpretation errors.

proposal.summary: Preserve the existing fetch-recovery guidance; refine discovery identity handling and incomplete-field recovery.

edits.title: Inspect discoveries and reconcile name variants
edits.content: Empty discovery placeholders caused stalled_search issues even when later calls recorded entities for the same queries. After each search, inspect its results and record actual newly discovered entities once; for search_many, do this separately for each query in input order. Do not emit [] before inspecting results or assume a later record erases an earlier empty event. Reconcile names against known entities before computing novelty: punctuation variants, added initials, shortened names, and unambiguous surnames can denote an already discovered entity. Keep an evidence-backed alias map; do not merge ambiguous names automatically. String inequality alone does not establish a new entity. Use [] honestly when no new entities were found, including verification searches that supply useful new field evidence. Do not invent discoveries to suppress a stall warning.

edits.title: Recover missing or incomplete fields from rendered pages
edits.content: When a model-rendered fetch returns usable but incomplete text, identify the specific missing or partial fields before fetching again. Request concise factual summaries for those fields, with brief supporting excerpts where needed, rather than full-page reproduction. Test the revised focus on one page and inspect whether it supplies the missing evidence before expanding. Preserve each fetched response with its URL and focus so later responses do not overwrite earlier support. Review populated cells as well as blanks: a summary or excerpt can pass quote-membership checks while omitting required scope or exact wording. Maintain unresolved field requirements separately from cell values; do not insert editorial gap notes into values or count a nonempty partial value as complete. Reuse saved evidence first, then retrieve targeted evidence for unresolved requirements. Keep unstated facts unresolved rather than inferring them from birthplace, institutional location, or ambiguous collective descriptions. Validate quotes against an individual saved response and separately check entity attribution, relevant time, and completeness. For shared statements, confirm applicability to each entity and avoid copying partner-specific framing that creates self-reference. After repair, repeat structural and semantic checks on the changed fields. This procedure applies to incomplete successful responses; FETCH_FAILED calls for bounded retries and source switching.

additional_candidates.description: Name variants were recorded as newly discovered entities because novelty used exact string comparison.
Semantic review and targeted retrieval repaired incomplete populated fields that passed quote-membership and missing-cell checks.

decisions.reason: All 16 occurrences concern follow-up verification: six year-level nationality queries, three targeted affiliation/nationality queries, four individual nationality queries, and three final audit queries. Their empty discovery records are consistent with researching already known entities, and several yielded useful field evidence. Initial discovery was recorded after inspection. Entry 0 already permits honest empty verification records; recurring signals alone do not demonstrate that guidance failed. The separate alias-novelty defect is addressed below.

Reviewed all 21 failures: ten initial same-site pages, two early alternative sources, five subsequent gap-research sources, two nationality sources, and two final audit sources. The run tracked attempted URLs, tested a small alternative batch, reused saved hits, and recovered through other sources without repeating failed URLs. Clean URLs and a PDF also failed, so URL formatting is not an established cause. Entry 1 already covers this failure mode and the observed recovery; its usage outcomes do not justify deletion or another edit.

The discoveries ledger counts shortened names, added middle initials, an apostrophe variant, and surnames as new entities after their full names were already recorded. The trajectory computes novelty through exact membership in known_names. Final rows avoid duplication, but discovery accounting remains misleading. Extend the existing discovery memory with evidence-backed alias reconciliation rather than create another entry.

Quote checks repeatedly passed while a motivation remained an excerpt; a later repair even produced a nonempty value containing an editorial gap note, so the missing-cell report showed no gaps. Semantic review identified the omitted scope, targeted retrieval supplied it, and final validation passed. Reviews also repaired partner-specific quotation framing. Extend the existing recovery skill with this successful review-and-repair procedure. Entry 2 has no usage outcomes, so this is an evidence-based extension, not a claim that it performed badly.
